definitions.gloss: curriculum; course of study; academic program
definitions.explanation: The organized plan of subjects and content that students follow at a school or university. Defines what is taught, in what order, and how much time is allocated.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{教科課程|きょうかかてい}が{来年度|らいねんど}から{導入|どうにゅう}される。
examples.english: A new curriculum will be introduced starting next academic year.

examples.japanese: この{大学|だいがく}の{教科課程|きょうかかてい}は{実践的|じっせんてき}な{内容|ないよう}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: This university's curriculum has a lot of practical content.

examples.japanese: {教科課程|きょうかかてい}の{改定|かいてい}に{伴|ともな}い、プログラミングが{必修科目|ひっしゅうかもく}に{加|くわ}わった。
examples.english: With the revision of the curriculum, programming was added as a required subject.

notes:
Composed of {教科|きょうか} (school subject) and {課程|かてい} (course, program). An educational administration term used in discussions about what schools teach and how education is structured.

USAGE:
More commonly seen as {教育課程|きょういくかてい} (education curriculum) in official documents. {教科課程|きょうかかてい} emphasizes the subject-based structure of the curriculum. Both terms appear in discussions about education reform, school management, and academic planning. The English loanword カリキュラム is also widely used.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {教科課程|きょうかかてい}を{編成|へんせい}する: to organize a curriculum
- {教科課程|きょうかかてい}の{改定|かいてい}: curriculum revision
- {教科課程|きょうかかてい}に{含|ふく}まれる: to be included in the curriculum
- {教科課程|きょうかかてい}を{修了|しゅうりょう}する: to complete a course of study

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {教育課程|きょういくかてい}: education curriculum — the broader, more official term used in government guidelines
- カリキュラム: curriculum — the English loanword, commonly used in both formal and informal contexts
- {学習指導要領|がくしゅうしどうようりょう}: Course of Study — the official national curriculum guidelines issued by Japan's Ministry of Education
- {科目|かもく}: subject, course — an individual class within the curriculum
